definition: a small, round piece of metal used as money

collocations.example: She paid the stall owner with an old gold coin.
Let's flip a coin to decide who goes first.

definition: to happen at the same time as something else

collocations.example: Our trade show will coincide with the city festival.
Their holidays happened to coincide, so they traveled together.

definition: to work together with others on a shared task

collocations.example: Our team will collaborate with a design firm abroad.
Two authors collaborated on the new textbook.

definition: a sudden and complete failure of something

collocations.example: The sudden economic collapse left thousands without work.
The company was on the verge of collapse last year.

definition: a person who works with you at the same job

collocations.example: She is a close colleague I have trusted for years.
A senior colleague reviewed my report before the meeting.

definition: a country or area ruled by another, more powerful country

collocations.example: The island was once a British colony.
The former colony gained independence in 1960.

definition: a regular piece of writing by one person in a newspaper or magazine

collocations.example: She writes a weekly column for the local paper.
He was hired to write a column about finance.

definition: to try hard to stop something bad from happening

collocations.example: New laws were passed to combat corruption in business.
The city hired more police to combat crime.

definition: a film, play, or show that is funny and makes people laugh

collocations.example: The new film is a light romantic comedy.
The theater staged a classic comedy last weekend.

definition: money paid to a salesperson based on how much they sell

collocations.example: She earns commission on every car she sells.
The salespeople here work on commission only.

definition: to share information or ideas with other people

collocations.example: Managers must communicate with their staff regularly.
Good leaders communicate effectively under pressure.

definition: a person who believes that property should be owned by the whole community

collocations.example: He remained a committed communist throughout his life.
The former communist later joined a new party.

definition: someone or something that spends time with you or travels with you

collocations.example: She was a pleasant travel companion on the long trip.
His old dog became his constant companion.

definition: to make up for a loss, often by paying money

collocations.example: The bonus helped compensate for the long hours.
The airline promised to fully compensate the passengers.

definition: to try to be more successful than someone else

collocations.example: Small shops struggle to compete with large chains.
Several firms are competing for the same contract.

definition: having enough skill or ability to do something well

collocations.example: She is a highly competent project manager.
The new engineer is technically competent and reliable.

definition: a statement that you are not happy about something

collocations.example: Several customers made a complaint about the slow service.
He filed a formal complaint with the manager.

definition: having many connected parts and difficult to understand

collocations.example: The team worked together to solve a complex problem.
The approval process is highly complex and slow.

definition: one of the parts that together make up a whole thing

collocations.example: Trust is a key component of good teamwork.
The factory makes electronic components for phones.

definition: to create a piece of music or writing

collocations.example: She was asked to compose music for the film.
He sat down to compose a letter of thanks.

definition: a substance made of two or more elements joined together

collocations.example: Water is a chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
Scientists studied the organic compound in the lab.

definition: including all or nearly all of something

collocations.example: The manager carried out a comprehensive review of costs.
The book is a comprehensive guide to basic grammar.

definition: to be made up of certain parts or members

collocations.example: The course comprises several short modules.
Older workers comprise a large part of the team.

definition: an agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wants

collocations.example: After hours of talks, the two sides reached a compromise.
Both teams accepted a reasonable compromise.

definition: to think of or imagine an idea or plan

collocations.example: It is hard to conceive of work life without email.
She conceived a plan to cut office costs.

definition: a general idea about something

collocations.example: Students must grasp the basic concept first.
Freedom is an abstract concept that is hard to define.

definition: a public event where music is performed

collocations.example: They attended a live concert downtown last night.
The orchestra played in a large concert hall.

definition: to decide something after thinking carefully

collocations.example: What can we conclude from these test results?
We can safely conclude that the plan worked.

definition: a decision reached after thinking about the facts

collocations.example: It is too early to draw a conclusion from the data.
That is the logical conclusion of the argument.

definition: based on facts, definite, and not just general ideas

collocations.example: The police had no concrete evidence against him.
Can you give a concrete example of the problem?

definition: to say strongly in public that something is very wrong

collocations.example: World leaders strongly condemn the attack.
The group publicly condemned the violence.

definition: to organize and carry out a particular activity

collocations.example: The university conducts research on clean energy.
The firm conducted a survey of its customers.

definition: to discuss something with other people before deciding

collocations.example: He wanted to confer with colleagues before deciding.
The managers conferred about the new budget.

definition: to admit that you have done something wrong

collocations.example: He confessed to taking the money from the drawer.
She finally confessed her crime to the police.

definition: the feeling of being sure about your own ability

collocations.example: The new employee slowly gained confidence at work.
She answered every question with quiet confidence.

definition: feeling sure that something good will happen or succeed

collocations.example: The manager is confident of a strong sales year.
The team felt quietly confident before the launch.

definition: to keep something within set limits

collocations.example: The illness confined her to bed for a week.
Please confine your comments to the main topic.

definition: to state that something is true or definite

collocations.example: Please confirm your booking by email today.
The office confirmed receipt of the documents.

definition: a serious disagreement between people or groups

collocations.example: The two departments had an ongoing conflict for months.
They worked hard to resolve the conflict quickly.

definition: to face a difficult problem and deal with it

collocations.example: Managers should confront workplace problems early and directly.
She boldly confronted her strongest critics.

definition: a large formal meeting of people from different groups

collocations.example: She presented her findings at a medical congress.
The international congress drew experts worldwide.

definition: permission for something to happen

collocations.example: You need written consent from a parent to join.
The patient gave consent for the surgery.

definition: a result that follows from an action or decision

collocations.example: The delay had serious consequences for the project.
He arrived late and, as a consequence, missed the meeting.

definition: happening as a direct result of something else

collocations.example: The flood and the consequent loss of crops hurt farmers.
The price rise was consequent on the fuel shortage.

definition: careful and avoiding risk or sudden change

collocations.example: The firm made a conservative estimate of sales.
They took a conservative approach to investing.

definition: to use something carefully so it is not wasted

collocations.example: Switch off the lights to conserve energy.
Farmers use drip systems to conserve water.

definition: large in amount, size, or importance

collocations.example: The project cost a considerable amount of money.
It took a considerable time to finish the report.

definition: to be made up of certain things or people

collocations.example: The team consists of five experienced members.
The meal mainly consists of rice and vegetables.

definition: always behaving or happening in the same way

collocations.example: The player gave a consistent performance all season.
Customers expect consistent quality from the brand.

definition: to be or to be counted as something

collocations.example: Such actions constitute a serious threat to safety.
Testing people without consent may constitute a crime.

definition: the basic set of laws by which a country is governed

collocations.example: The country has a written constitution.
The assembly was asked to draft a constitution.

definition: to limit or hold back what someone can do

collocations.example: High costs severely constrain the small business.
A lack of funds constrained the company's growth.

definition: to build something by putting parts together

collocations.example: Workers will construct a new office building here.
She constructed a small model of the bridge.

definition: to ask someone for advice or information

collocations.example: You should consult with a lawyer before signing.
Consult a doctor if the pain continues.

definition: to use up an amount of something such as energy or fuel

collocations.example: Older machines consume far more energy.
The new engine consumes much less fuel.

definition: the amount of something that is used up

collocations.example: The factory reduced its energy consumption last year.
The small car has very low fuel consumption.

definition: belonging to the present time; modern

collocations.example: The gallery mostly displays contemporary art.
New technology deeply shapes contemporary society today.

definition: to argue or claim that something is true

collocations.example: Critics contend that the new plan will fail.
The economists strongly contend the opposite view.

definition: the ideas or information contained in a book, course, or website

collocations.example: The course content covers basic business grammar.
The company produces digital content for websites.

definition: an event in which people compete to win

collocations.example: She decided to enter a writing contest.
He won first prize in a singing contest.

definition: the situation that helps explain something

collocations.example: In this context, the decision makes good sense.
The novel reflects its cultural context well.

definition: one of the large land masses of the earth

collocations.example: The disease spread across the entire continent.
Early explorers mapped the vast continent slowly.

definition: to say the opposite of what someone else has said

collocations.example: He kept contradicting himself during the talk.
Her story flatly contradicts the official report.

definition: a clear difference between two things

collocations.example: There is a sharp contrast between the two plans.
In contrast, sales rose sharply last year.

definition: public disagreement about something over a long time

collocations.example: The new policy caused a lot of controversy.
The decision became a major political controversy.

definition: a large formal meeting of people with shared interests

collocations.example: The company holds an annual sales convention.
Thousands of dealers attended the convention.

definition: to change something from one form or use to another

collocations.example: They converted the old barn into offices.
The software can convert data into clear charts.

definition: to communicate ideas or feelings to others

collocations.example: Clear graphs help convey information to readers.
Her tone conveyed a strong message of warning.

definition: to officially decide in court that someone is guilty

collocations.example: The court convicted him of fraud.
An innocent man was wrongly convicted.

definition: to work together with someone toward a shared aim

collocations.example: The firm agreed to cooperate with investigators.
Staff must cooperate fully with the new rules.

definition: to organize different parts so they work well together

collocations.example: She will coordinate with the other departments.
The teams coordinated their efforts very well.

definition: the central and most important part of something

collocations.example: The company decided to focus on its core business.
Teamwork lies at the core of our success.

definition: relating to a large company or business

collocations.example: The firm has a friendly corporate culture.
The board approved the new corporate strategy.

definition: to have a close connection with something else

collocations.example: Income does not always correlate with happiness.
The two sets of figures closely correlate.

definition: to match or be similar to something else

collocations.example: The numbers correspond to the items on the list.
His account closely corresponds with the records.

definition: a journalist who reports news from a particular place or subject

collocations.example: She works as a foreign correspondent in Tokyo.
The war correspondent sent daily reports home.

definition: a long narrow passage inside a building

collocations.example: They walked along the long corridor to the exit.
Her office is just down the corridor.

definition: using power dishonestly for personal gain

collocations.example: The corrupt official was caught taking bribes.
The company was accused of corrupt practices.

definition: advice given carefully to someone

collocations.example: He always valued her wise counsel.
She sought counsel from an experienced mentor.

definition: the ability to face danger or difficulty without fear

collocations.example: She showed great courage during the crisis.
It took moral courage to speak out against the plan.

definition: an activity that needs skill in making things by hand

collocations.example: Pottery is a traditional craft in this region.
She teaches arts and crafts to young children.

definition: the people who work together on a ship, plane, or project

collocations.example: Every crew member wore a life jacket.
The flight crew welcomed passengers aboard.

definition: a time of great difficulty or danger

collocations.example: The financial crisis hurt many local families.
The team worked hard to deal with the crisis.

definition: the standards used to judge or decide something

collocations.example: The selection criteria were clearly listed online.
Only two candidates meet the criteria for the job.

definition: a person whose job is to review books, films, or art

collocations.example: She works as a film critic for a magazine.
The art critic praised the new exhibition.

definition: to say what you think is wrong about someone or something

collocations.example: Reviewers strongly criticised the new plan.
They criticised the manager for the long delay.

definition: remarks that say what is wrong with someone or something

collocations.example: The report faced harsh criticism from the public.
She welcomed constructive criticism from her boss.

definition: a plant grown in large amounts for food

collocations.example: Farmers here grow a crop of wheat each year.
The drought caused a serious crop failure.

definition: extremely important for the success of something

collocations.example: She played a crucial role in the project.
Price is a crucial factor for most buyers.

definition: a holiday spent traveling by ship

collocations.example: They boarded the cruise ship at noon.
The couple decided to go on a cruise.

definition: to press something hard so it breaks or is damaged

collocations.example: Crush the ice before adding it to the drinks.
The recipe says to crush two cloves of garlic.

definition: very clear, high-quality glass

collocations.example: The wine glasses are made of fine lead crystal.
She placed the flowers in a crystal vase.

definition: the money used in a particular country

collocations.example: You can exchange foreign currency at the bank.
All prices are shown in the local currency.

definition: the set of subjects taught in a school or course

collocations.example: Music is part of the school curriculum here.
The subject was added to the national curriculum.

definition: a piece of cloth hung to cover a window

collocations.example: She drew the curtains as it grew dark.
The heavy curtains kept the bright room dark.

definition: a line or shape that bends smoothly

collocations.example: There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The path followed a gentle curve down the hill.

definition: a traditional way of behaving that people have followed for a long time

collocations.example: Visitors should always respect local customs here.
The festival follows an ancient custom.

definition: a set of events that happen again and again in the same order

collocations.example: Scientists study the life cycle of insects.
The economy follows a regular business cycle.

definition: used informally to show that you are annoyed about something

collocations.example: This damn thing keeps breaking down.
The delay was a real damn nuisance.

definition: slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way

collocations.example: Wipe the table with a damp cloth.
The towels were still slightly damp this morning.
